Oral Judgment (Per Ms Sonak J):-
1. Heard learned Counsel for the parties.
2. Rule.
The Rule is made returnable immediately at the request of and with the consent of the learned Counsel for the parties.
3. The Petitioners seek the following substantive reliefs by instituting this Petition.

"(a) This Hon'ble Court be pleased to issue appropriate writ, order or direction including appropriate order of declaration that Corrigendum dt 4.6.2019 and Conveyance Deed dt 6.8.2019 is invalid in law and does not take effect in law and is void document.

(b) This Hon'ble Court by appropriate writ, order or direction declare the Deed of Conveyance dt 16.3.2019 of Barrack Nos. 1257&1258, CTS No. 17282 to 17308, Sheet No. 4, Ulhasnagar-4 adm 1453 5/9 sq yds is binding on Respondents and cannot be nullified by unilateral act of Respondents"

sentences.text: On 5 September 2019, when this matter was taken up for admission, time was granted to the learned AGP to take instructions, and the matter was listed on 26 September 2019.
Until then, the parties were directed to maintain the status quo.
5. Mr Agarwal, the learned Counsel for the Petitioners states that this status quo order made on 5 September 2019 has continued till date.
6. The record shows that Petitioner's land admeasuring 8855.5/9 sq. yards, was acquired by the State Government for the Police Department.

Upon such acquisition, the Petitioners claimed relief under the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 ("said Act").
7.
Initially, no relief was granted to the Petitioners, and therefore, the Petitioners were constrained to institute a Revision Petition under Section 24 of the Act.
The Revisional Authority disposed of this Revision Petition vide a detailed judgment and order dated 27 December 2016.

8. The operative portion of the Revisional Authority's order dated 27 December 2016 reads as follows:-
ORDER 1. The Revision Application is partly allowed.
2. The Order cum letter No. SDO/c-5/Plot/WS-225 dated 22nd November 2002 passed by the Sub-Divisional Officer Cum Managing Officer, Ulhasnagar Division,
Ulhasnagar is hereby set aside.
3. The matter is remanded back to the Sub-Divisional Officer Cum Managing Officer,
Ulhasnagar Division, Ulhasnagar for enquiry giving sufficient opportunity to the Sakharam Tukaram Patil & Ors v Managin cum sub Divisional Officer, Ulhasnagar sub-divisional Powai & Ors.
17-aswp-9818-2019-J(F).docx Revision Applicant of being heard and for submission of evidence in view of the above mentioned observations and pass the order in accordance with the provisions of Govt. Resolutions and Circulars from time to time especially Govt.

sentences.text: 3 9. Based on the above remand order by the Revisional Authority, the Sub Divisional Officer cum Managing Officer, Ulhasnagar Division, Ulhasnagar, enquired into the matter and made an order dated 20 February 2018.
The Petitioners were granted liberty to apply for alternate land by this order.
The Petitioners accordingly applied for alternate land after identifying the same.

10. Ultimately, by way of alternate land, a Conveyance Deed dated 16 March 2019 was executed,
conveying in favour of the Petitioners the property/lands described in Schedule I of the Conveyance.
This Conveyance Deed is at Exhibit 'G' and is a part of the paper book.

11. Schedule I, which describes the allotted alternate property, reads as follows:-
Schedule I All that piece and parcel of land situated at Portion of CTS No. 25220 &
Portion of CTS No. 28218, Sheet No.75, Ulhasnagar- Sakharam Tukaram Patil & Ors v Managin cum sub Divisional Officer, Ulhasnagar sub-divisional Powai & Ors.
17-aswp-9818-2019-J(F).docx 5 containing by admeasurments 500 sq. Yards (Five hundred sq. yards.) (418 Sq. meter) or thereabouts and bounded.
12.
The above allotment was made, and conveyance executed only after the Petitioners paid an amount of Rs 10,71,678/-.
The Petitioners have placed on record the receipt towards payment of this amount.
13. The Petitioner's case is that under the conveyance dated 16 March 2016, the Petitioners took possession of the allotted land.

However, at that stage, the Senior Police Inspector of Vitthalwadi Police Station prevented the Petitioners from undertaking any activities on the allotted land by stating that this property belongs to the Vitthalwadi Police Station.

14. The Petitioners have pleaded, and records bear that after this, the Sub Divisional Officer cum Managing Officer, Ulhasnagar Division, Ulhasnagar issued the impugned corrigendum dated 4 June 2019, which was followed by a Deed of Conveyance dated 6 August 2019.
Even before these documents were issued, the Vitthalwadi Police took over the property.
All this was done without giving the Petitioners any notice or opportunity of hearing.

15. The impugned corrigendum dated 4 June 2019 at Exhibit 'I' (page 60) reads as follows:-
CORRIGENDUM

As per Hon Divisional Commissioner Kokan Bhavan Mumbai &
Hon. Authorised Chief Settlement Commissioner Mumbai Order

. The Conveyance Deed issued No.1257 & 1258, CTS No.17282 to CTS No.17308, Sheet No.4,
Ulhasnagar 4 for area Adm 1453.3/9 sq. yads in favour of Smt Shobha Vasant Sakharam Tukaram Patil & Ors v Managin cum sub Divisional Officer, Ulhasnagar sub-divisional Powai & Ors.

Managing Officer & Sub Divisional Officer Ulhasnagar Sub Division Ulhasnagar 16.

From the reading of the impugned corrigendum, we got the impression that only a part of the area allegedly in possession of the Vitthalwadi Police Station from out of the total allotted area of 1453.3/9 sq. yards was excluded.
However, on reading the conveyance dated 6 August 2019, we now find that the entire land allotted to the Petitioners is now sought to be allotted to the Police Commissioner.
17. Thus, the Petitioners, upon obtaining a favourable order under the Displaced Persons (Compensation and Rehabilitation) Act, 1954 were allotted land admeasuring 1438.3/9 sq. yards.
The conveyance was also executed after collecting an amount of Rs 10,71,678/- from the Petitioners.

Within a few days, however, without even minimum compliance with principles of natural justice and fair play and without indicating the source of power under which such action was taken, the Respondents, by issuing a corrigendum, have virtually taken away the entire allotted land from the Petitioners.

This is a high-handed action on the part of the Respondents.
18.
In any event, the above action should have been preceded by minimum compliance with the principles of natural justice and fair play.
The impugned action visits the Petitioners with serious civil consequences.

The land allotted Sakharam Tukaram Patil & Ors v Managin cum sub Divisional Officer, Ulhasnagar sub-divisional Powai & Ors.
17-aswp-9818-2019-J(F).docx in their favour and for which even a conveyance was issued has been sought to be summarily taken away.

sentences.text: The compensation paid by the Petitioners is retained, and there is no offer to return the same.
The conveyance issued in favour of the Petitioners has virtually been nullified by issuing a corrigendum.
Therefore, we are constrained to observe that this is nothing but some high-handed action not authorised by law.

19. On the above ground, we quash and set aside the corrigendum dated 4 June 2019 and the Conveyance Deed dated 6 August 2019 and restore the Petitioners Conveyance Deed dated 16 March 2019 by which the Petitioners were allotted and is vested with property admeasuring 1453.3/9 sq.
yards.

20. The Respondents must immediately restore the property, which is the subject matter of the Deed of Conveyance dated 16 March 2019, to the Petitioners and not obstruct the Petitioners from undertaking any activities therein.
This restoration must be done within eight weeks from today.
A compliance report with photographs must be filed in this Court by 28 February 2025 after serving an advance copy on the Counsel for the Petitioners.
21. However, this order will not preclude the Respondents from taking appropriate action as is permissible under the law about the allotment and conveyance favouring the Petitioners.

Accordingly, leave is granted to make this correction in prayer clause (b).

23. The Rule is made absolute regarding prayer clauses (a) and amended prayer clauses (b).
